content_metadata.description: This tutorial video serves as an introduction to using Orange software. It provides viewers with a walkthrough of the Orange interface, demonstrates widget functionality, and guides users through building their first data analysis workflow. The video maintains a positive and approachable tone throughout, with Ida as the narrator and guide. By the end of the video, viewers have successfully built a simple workflow and are empowered to explore further.

trimmingSuggestions.description: The welcome screen segment could be shortened, focusing on only the "New" button. The other options can be explained later when relevant.
The Data Table display could be trimmed. Briefly showing the table is enough to illustrate its purpose.

text_to_speech: Hello and welcome to Orange tutorials. My name is Ajda and I'll be your guide in the world of Data Science. Let's dig in. You have probably already downloaded and installed Orange. If not, you will find the detailed installation guide in the link below. When you open Orange, the first thing you will see is a welcome screen. From here you can start a new data analysis workflow, open a recent one or explore tutorials. Ok, let's exit the welcome screen. Orange starts with a blank canvas. This is where all the magic will take place. But every magic needs some secret ingredients. Our ingredients are called widgets. Widgets are computational units of Orange. They read the data, process it, visualize it do clustering, build predictive models and otherwise help you to explore the data. You will find them on the left hand side of the screen. Most data analysis workflows begin with a File widget with which we load our data. Click on the File widget and it will appear in the canvas. Open it with a double-click. Go to Browse documentation data sets and load one of the existing data files that come with Orange. You can, naturally, load your own data but for the sake of simplicity let's go with a famous Iris data set. Now we would like to see what we've just loaded. Click on the Data Table and the widget will appear in canvas. Widgets communicate with one another. They have an input channel, an output channel or both. To feed the data from the File widget to the Data Table, drag a line from the right, output side of the File widget to the left, input side of the Data Table widget. Now, open the Data Table. Wow, that's a lot of numbers in columns and rows. Let's instead plot the data. We will use Scatter Plot and connect it with the File widget. Much better! And with this, you just set up your first workflow. Congratulations!
